event_summary: 1897年、23歳のラフマニノフが発表した交響曲第1番の初演は、不出来な指揮も重なり大失敗に終わった。彼は深く傷つき、1917年の亡命の際に楽譜をロシアに残したまま二度と演奏しようとしなかったが、死後の1944年に各楽器のパート譜だけが偶然発見され、翌1945年モスクワで甦った。

He wears a dark formal suit jacket with a crisp white collared shirt and a dark necktie, exactly as in the reference image. Bust-to-shoulder composition, facing forward toward the viewer. middle_slides.text: 1897年、23歳のセルゲイ・ラフマニノフは渾身の交響曲第1番を発表したが、指揮の出来も悪く初演は惨憺たる失敗に終わった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration of a young Sergei Rachmaninoff at age 23 in 1897: the same elongated angular face, high cheekbones, deep-set pale grey-blue eyes and long straight nose as his iconic portrait, but younger and smoother-skinned, with a fuller head of dark hair and no visible receding hairline, clean-shaven. He stands rigid and stricken near the edge of a grand ornate 19th-century Russian concert hall stage, dressed in a formal black tailcoat with white bow tie, illuminated by dim stage light while in the shadowy background a podium and orchestra chairs sit abandoned; his expression is one of quiet devastation and humiliation, shoulders slumped, eyes lowered. Painterly oil-painting brushwork, warm candlelit tones mixed with cold shadow, cinematic composition, not photorealistic, no text.

middle_slides.text: 深く傷ついたラフマニノフは、1917年に祖国を離れる際この交響曲の楽譜をロシアに残していき、曲は長い沈黙の中に消えていった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration of Sergei Rachmaninoff in 1917, now in his mid-forties with the same elongated angular face, high forehead, short dark hair receding at the temples, deep-set pale eyes and clean-shaven jaw as his iconic portrait, now with a touch more grey at the temples and a careworn, solemn expression. He is shown from behind walking away through a snowy railway platform toward a waiting train, wearing a long dark overcoat and hat, a suitcase in hand, while a few loose sheets of music manuscript paper lie scattered and abandoned on a bench behind him; seen from behind, face not visible, body fully turned away. Muted wintry blues and greys, painterly oil texture, cinematic composition, not photorealistic, no text.

middle_slides.text: 1944年、彼の死の翌年、紛失していた総譜の代わりに各楽器のパート譜が、レニングラード音楽院の資料庫で偶然発見されたのだった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration symbolizing the 1944 rediscovery of lost orchestral parts: a dusty archive room in a conservatory, tall wooden shelves stacked with aged manuscript folders and yellowed sheet music, soft beam of light falling on a bundle of orchestral parts tied with string on a table. On the wall above hangs a framed painted portrait of Sergei Rachmaninoff as in his iconic likeness, elongated angular face, high forehead, short dark hair greying at the temples, deep-set pale eyes, clean-shaven, solemn expression, gazing down over the scene as if watching from afar; no other people present. Warm sepia and amber tones, painterly oil brushwork, cinematic composition, not photorealistic, no text.

middle_slides.text: 1945年、死後わずか2年で交響曲第1番はモスクワで甦り、再評価の末、今では世界中のオーケストラが演奏する名曲となった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustration of a jubilant 1945 Moscow concert hall at the triumphant revival of the Symphony No. 1: a grand ornate hall filled with warm golden light, an orchestra mid-performance and a sense of applause and energy, and high above the stage, painted as if glowing softly like a translucent portrait on the hall's ceiling mural, the face of Sergei Rachmaninoff watching over the scene—elongated angular face, high forehead, short dark hair greying at the temples, deep-set pale eyes, clean-shaven, a faint serene expression replacing his old sorrow. No other distinct figures, only the orchestra implied in soft silhouette. Rich warm palette, painterly oil brushwork, cinematic composition, not photorealistic, no text.

fb_caption:
なぜラフマニノフは、渾身の交響曲を自ら封印してしまったのでしょうか。23歳での初演大失敗から半世紀近くを経て、楽譜なき名曲は思わぬ形で蘇ります。🎵

「忙しい大人のためのクラシック音楽ノート」では、忙しい日々の合間に、
ほんの数分だけ立ち止まりたくなる、クラシック音楽の物語を発信しています。
指揮者マエストロ・ノートが案内する、作曲家たちの知られざる人生の
ドラマ——栄光の裏にあった挫折、常識をくつがえす意外な真実——を、
毎日少しずつお届けしています。

難しい知識は必要ありません。ただ、物語として楽しんでいただければ、
それだけで十分です。

YouTubeでは、この作曲家の物語を動画でもお届けしています。https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yTmvr3Gl02M
